title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (People Ops Extended)
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook reference for engineers, product, and operations teams joining or working at Redwood Inference. It consolidates expectations for working at Redwood, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding flows, and a compact internal tools guide. This page is intended for broad internal distribution and is maintained by People Ops.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

- Mission-oriented: we prioritize reliability, performance, and developer experience; individual work should map back to measurable customer outcomes.
- Core values: Act like an owner; Ship with quality; Be data-informed; Be kind and curious.
- Work model: hybrid-first with optional remote teams by agreement. Core collaboration hours are 10:00–16:00 PT for cross-team syncs.

2) Roles & career ladders (high-level)

Overview: Redwood maintains two primary progression paths: Individual Contributor (IC) and Manager. Ladders exist for Engineering, Product, SRE, Applied ML, and Developer Experience. Each ladder defines responsibilities, impact, scope, and example competencies.

- IC track (engineering examples):
  - E1 (New grad / Junior): contributes to scoped tasks, learns codebase and systems.
  - E2 (Software Engineer): delivers features, owns tickets end-to-end, participates in design reviews and on-call rotation.
  - E3 (Senior): owns significant components, drives design and incident response, mentors others and leads design reviews.
  - E4 (Staff): cross-team influence, architecture ownership, leads large technical initiatives and system-wide improvements.
  - E5+ (Principal/Distinguished): sets long-term technical direction, represents Redwood externally, influences product strategy.

- Manager track:
  - M1 (Engineering Manager / Product Manager): manages small teams, coaches reports, runs 1:1s, and conducts performance reviews.
  - M2 (Senior Manager): managers of managers, owns multi-team outcomes, hiring bar, and cross-functional delivery.

Competencies & promotion guidance:
- Promotions are based on demonstrated impact, scale of ownership, and consistent competency over time. Evidence includes design docs, launched projects, measurable product/customer metrics, and peer/manager feedback. Use the Career Ladder checklist (linked in related pages) and prepare a promotion packet at least six weeks before the next promotion cycle.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

- Compensation: competitive market base + equity grants and annual calibration. Compensation bands are documented by level; managers and People Ops can provide band guidance confidentially.
- Health & wellbeing: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision; company-paid basic life/AD&D; voluntary supplemental plans and commuter benefits where available.
- Time off: 20 days PTO starting year one (pro-rated), 10 paid company holidays, and flexible paid time off policies. Parental leave: up to 18 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (policy updated 2025).
- Remote & co-working stipend: monthly remote work stipend and optional co-working reimbursement for eligible locations.
- Learning & development: $2,000 annual learning stipend per employee plus team training budgets for conferences and certifications.
- Perks: commuter/childcare stipend (region-dependent), wellness reimbursement, ergonomic budget, and regular company retreats.

4) Hiring process & candidate experience (People Ops + Hiring Managers)

High-level steps:
1. Requisition & role brief: Hiring manager creates role brief and recommended level; People Ops posts the role and approves JD.
2. Sourcing & initial screen: Recruiter completes phone screen and coordinates technical pre-screen.
3. Interview loop: 4–5 interviews including a technical coding/design/problem-solving interview, product sense or role-specific interview, leadership/culture interview, and a hiring manager conversation. Standardized rubrics are attached to each public role.
4. Debrief & decision: Interviewers submit feedback within 48 hours; hiring manager convenes a calibrated debrief.
5. Offer & checks: People Ops prepares offer packet, equity grant paperwork, and runs background checks where required.
6. Acceptance & pre-boarding: Recruiter coordinates start date and pre-boarding activities.

Interview rubric highlights:
- Use objective scoring (1–5) on technical ability, problem decomposition, communication, impact, and culture fit. Document reasons for disqualification and avoid illegal or inappropriate questions.

5) Onboarding overview & 30-60-90 plan

Pre-boarding (1–2 weeks before start):
- IT & access: request laptop, provision SSO account, add to org chart and Slack, and enroll in benefits.
- Pre-read: team roadmap, architecture overview, key repositories, and security training links.

Day 0–30 (orientation & ramp):
1. Orientation: company values, benefits walkthrough, HR paperwork, security and compliance training.
2. Team onboarding: meet with manager for 30-60-90 goals, buddy assignment, codebase walkthrough, and first small ticket.
3. Access checklist (example table):
   - Laptop provisioning | Owner: IT | Target: Day -3 | Status: Completed
   - SSO + email | Owner: IT/Security | Target: Day 0 | Status: Completed
   - Slack + PagerDuty | Owner: Manager/Oncall lead | Target: Day 1 | Status: In progress
   - Repo access (git) | Owner: Team lead | Target: Day 3 | Status: Pending
   - Dev environment | Owner: Mentor | Target: Day 7 | Status: Pending

Day 30–90 (impact & independence):
- Deliver first project (bug fix or small feature) and present solution in a team demo.
- Participate in on-call shadowing (for SRE/infra roles) and review incident runbooks.
- Career conversation: manager and new hire set goals for the next 6–12 months.

6) Onboarding checklist (numbered procedure)

1. Complete HR paperwork and benefits enrollment within first seven days.
2. Finish mandatory security and data handling training by day 14.
3. Confirm access to required systems (GitHub, CI, cloud console, Jira, Slack) by day 7 — escalate missing access to it-ops@redwood.com.
4. Complete first code review and merge a non-trivial PR by day 30.
5. Schedule 1:1 cadence with manager (weekly for first three months).

7) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

- Slack: primary collaboration channel. Join #all, #engineering, and your team channel. Use threads for discussions and pin important resources.
- GitHub: source of truth for code. Follow branching and PR templates and use required code owners where applicable.
- Jira: issue tracking and sprint boards. Create Epics for large initiatives and link PRs to Jira tickets.
- CI/CD (CircleCI and GitHub Actions): pipelines run on push to main; see cd/README.md for deployment steps and rollback guidance.
- Datadog & Grafana: observability dashboards and alerting. Dashboards per service are stored in the Dashboards folder; create read-only dashboards for cross-team reviews.
- PagerDuty: on-call scheduling and incident paging. Follow the on-call runbook for first responder steps and escalation policy.
- Confluence: authoritative documentation, architecture decisions, and runbooks. Use the design doc template when proposing significant changes.
- HRIS & ATS (Workday/Greenhouse integrations): benefits, time-off, and payroll records.

Access & onboarding for tools:
- Request access via the Self-Service portal (link in People Ops page). Typical SLA: 72 hours. For urgent access (on-call starting week one), tag request with URGENT and email it-ops@redwood.com.

8) Ownership & contacts

- Document owner: People Ops (Ava Chen). For updates, open a doc PR or email people-ops@redwood.com.
- Hiring escalation: Senior Recruiter (Priya Singh) for offer or candidate issues; Legal for international hire questions.
- Security & compliance: Security team (security@redwood.com) maintains data handling training and audit checklists.

9) Policies & related references

- See company policies for parental leave, flexible work, reimbursement limits, and compensation banding. Use the related pages links above to find level-specific guidance and the detailed onboarding playbook.

Appendix: Promotion checklist (example items)

- 2+ peer nomination emails describing impact.
- 3–5 technical artifacts (design docs, code samples, release notes).
- Performance review notes for the past 12 months.
- Manager endorsement with proposed new scope and band.

Review cadence: This handbook is reviewed quarterly and updated to reflect changes in benefits, role definitions, tooling, or compliance requirements. For corrections or questions, contact people-ops@redwood.com.
